title: Global trust deficits are becoming an operating constraint on diplomacy, technology, trade, security, and shared public goods
source_unit: Stimson Center, Doha Forum, and Global Institute for Strategic Research, Future of International Cooperation Report 2026: Redefining Global Trust
geography: Global and regional governance, with perspectives spanning diplomacy, economics, technology, security, justice, and the Global South

observations.period: September 2026; global trust and international cooperation diagnosis

denominator.unit: global policy and governance synthesis; no single survey denominator

trust_domains.value: trust deficits are examined across global and regional politics, economics and technology, and security and justice

trust_mechanism.value: mistrust and distrust impede accurate information sharing, lower respect for international law, erode community and undermine belief in global public goods

observations.method: Co-produced policy report based on global and regional governance analysis, expert contributions, policy dialogues, institutional review, and proposals connected to the Summit of the Future, World Social Summit, financing-for-development and post-2030 agendas.
observations.uncertainty: This is a normative and strategic policy synthesis, not a representative trust survey, causal estimate, or independent evaluation of the proposed governance reforms.
observations.subgroup: States, regional organizations, civil society, business, technology actors, media, religious leaders, international organizations, and communities affected by global public-good and security decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Trust is not the only condition of cooperation: interests, material capacity, enforcement, power asymmetries and institutional design can enable or constrain cooperation even when confidence is low.

observations.period: 2026; proposed multilateral responses to information, AI, security and economic trust gaps

information_integrity_proposal.value: a Multilateral Information Integrity Council to assess information-environment degradation, develop shared standards and coordinate international responses

ai_capacity_proposal.value: a Global AI Hub and shared computing infrastructure to improve access to computing, data, expertise and knowledge-sharing for developing countries

preventive_diplomacy_proposal.value: an inter-regional early-warning and preventive-diplomacy network to monitor political erosion and engage before conflict escalates

trade_and_security_proposals.value: deeper inter-regional trade cooperation and clearer compliance, monitoring and dispute-resolution mechanisms in regional security arrangements

observations.method: Report recommendations linking information integrity, AI infrastructure, preventive diplomacy, trade cooperation, security compliance, accountability and post-2030 development planning.
observations.uncertainty: Proposals are not funded implementation plans; their feasibility, distributional effects, geopolitical acceptance, institutional mandate and measurable outcomes remain open.
observations.subgroup: Developing countries facing AI-capacity gaps, regional organizations, UN bodies, technology and business actors, conflict-affected populations, and states participating in multilateral governance.
observations.counterinterpretation: New global councils or hubs could add institutional duplication, contestation or centralization; regional and national capacity-building may sometimes be more credible than global coordination.

Official 81-page Future of International Cooperation Report 2026 PDF.

boundary: This record adds a global-governance trust route connecting information integrity, AI capacity, diplomacy, trade, security, justice, accountability and shared public goods. It is a normative policy synthesis, not a global trust prevalence estimate, a geopolitical forecast, a country implementation audit, or respondent-level data.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Stimson landing page, executive summary and 81-page PDF were reviewed; report scope, trust diagnosis, governance principles, and information-integrity, AI, preventive-diplomacy, trade and security proposals were cross-checked.
